assessment_summary: The proof correctly handles the cases where p = -∞ or q = ∞, and states the definition for the mean when p = 0 or q = 0. However, in line 0040, it makes the logical claim that "It remains to resolve the inequality for p, q \in \R_{\ge 0}". This falsely asserts that all cases outside of \R_{\ge 0} have been resolved. In reality, cases involving finite negative exponents (e.g., p = -1, q = 1) were never proven. This premature restriction incorrectly narrows the scope of the proof, representing a clear logical gap and making line 0040 the first flawed step.
counterexample: Let p = -1 and q = 1 (with x_k > 0). The inequality for these values has not been resolved by the preceding steps, which only addressed the infinite cases and stated the definition for 0. Since p = -1 is not in \R_{\ge 0}, the claim that it only remains to resolve the inequality for p, q \in \R_{\ge 0} is logically false.
